title: If a battery starts to fail
summary: Your safety matters more than the phone.
rules: Warning signs are hissing, smoke, a sweet or chemical smell, or sudden heat.
If you can do it safely, drop the battery into a metal container of dry sand.
Move away and let fresh air in. Do not breathe the smoke.
If there is a fire, leave the room and call emergency services.

title: Static electricity (ESD)
summary: Static can damage a chip without you feeling anything, and the fault may only appear later.
rules: Work on an anti-static mat when you can.
Wear a grounded wrist strap, or touch grounded metal before touching a board.
Avoid carpets and synthetic clothes while you work.
Hold boards by their edges.
Keep loose parts on the mat, not on plastic bags.

title: Lithium battery safety
summary: A damaged battery can start a fire, even minutes after the damage.
rules: Let the battery run down to below 25% before you remove it.
Disconnect the battery before you work on anything else.
Use plastic tools only around the battery.
Never puncture, bend, crush or directly heat a battery.
Never charge or keep using a swollen battery. Take it to a repair shop.
Fit only a battery made for your exact model, from a seller you trust.
Tape the old connector and take the battery to an e-waste collection point. Never put it in household trash.

title: Heat, glass and chemicals
summary: Most injuries come from hot surfaces and sharp edges.
rules: Wear safety glasses for every repair.
Keep heat moving and on the edges of the phone.
Let heated parts cool before you hold them.
Wear gloves around broken glass, and wrap old glass before you throw it away.
Isopropyl alcohol is flammable. Keep it away from heat tools and use it in a ventilated place.
Work at a clear table, never on a bed, sofa or carpet.
